physdesc.extent: 4 boxes (3 letter document containers and 1 legal document container)

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Reprints, reports, Ph.D. theses, and books created by Ford Foundation Fellowship recipients in Economic Development and Administration.

bioghist.head: Biographical / Historical
bioghist.p: Beginning in the 1956-1957 academic year, the Ford Foundation began offering fellowships to faculty and students in the field of economics and business administration. Fellowship candidates were nominated by universities at the invitation of the Foundation and selections were made with the assistance of advisory committees composed of faculty members. There were several categories of fellowships. Fellowships were awarded to MBA graduates seeking further study, doctoral students writing their dissertation, faculty pursuing research in Economics and Business Administration, and faculty seeking one year of study in mathematics, statistics, or the social sciences other than economics.

accessrestrict.head: Conditions Governing Access
accessrestrict.p: Open for research with select materials restricted as noted. Brittle or damaged items are available at the discretion of RAC.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: The collection is arranged alphabetically into one series:

userestrict.head: Conditions Governing Use
userestrict.p: Ford Foundation has title, copyright and literary rights in the collection, in so far as it holds them.

The Rockefeller Archive Center has authority to grant permission to cite and publish material from the collection. Permission to publish extensive excerpts, or material in its entirety, will be referred to the Ford Foundation.

acqinfo.head: Immediate Source of Acquisition
acqinfo.p: This material was transferred to RAC in 2019 by the Ford Foundation and ingested by RAC as Accession 2019:013.
